calls.head: The Golden Knights should tilt the ice
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Golden Knights have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Predators near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Golden Knights’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.head: Where the Golden Knights have the edge: shot suppression
calls.body: The Golden Knights are near the top of the league for shot suppression, and the Predators are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

surprises.head: Vegas shut down Nashville’s power play
surprises.body: Vegas has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Nashville’s power play created 1.1 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.5 (about 6.4 against Vegas) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: The Predators make it seven straight
paras: Ryan O'Reilly got the scoring started for the Predators early in the first, but Victor Olofsson made it 1-1 for Vegas less than four minutes later. Rasmus Andersson put the Golden Knights ahead 2-1 midway through the second. O'Reilly scored his second of the night midway through the third to tie it 2-2. The shootout went four rounds, and Roman Josi won it for the Preds after Filip Forsberg had scored earlier.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Golden Knights hit three posts and still lost. Juuse Saros made 40 saves for the Predators, and Adin Hill kept the Golden Knights in it, stopping 30 of 32. The Predators moved to 11-4-5, second in the Central, while the Golden Knights fell to 13-5-3, second in the Pacific.

items.text: The Predators are rolling: seven straight wins.
